newsitem.title: USA: Aon '96 results boosted by acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Aon '96 results boosted by acquisitions.

text.p: Aon Corp said Tuesday its 1996 fourth-quarter and full-year operating results benefited from a successful acquisition program and internal growth initiatives that focus on specialized lines of business and interdependent operation.

It cited inclusion of Bain Hogg Group, acquired early in the fourth quarter, and strong international growth. Aon said partially offsetting these results were pressures experienced in the reinsurance brokerage business, reflecting the continued difficult operating environment.
Aon said its insurance underwriting businesses generated eight percent revenue growth in 1996 to $1.8 billion. Pretax operating income before special charges rose seven percent to $264 million.

The insurance services holding company earlier Tuesday reported fourth-quarter operating income from continuing operations of $0.71 a share compared to $0.52 before special charges. During the quarter, Aon recorded restructuring charges of $60.3 million related to its acquisition of Bain Hogg.
Aon's stock was trading up 3/8 at 64-1/4.
